id.description: Catalog path, prefixed evc/: jurisdiction/classification slug, or a group's bare slug

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or EU, suffixed with a state or province's ISO 3166-2 code, e.g. US-CA; a group, which classifications from any jurisdiction can name, has none

jurisdiction_name.description: What labels call the jurisdiction, e.g. California; a law with class_3_throttle false needs one

groups.description: The shared classifications whose definition this one fits, by their ids; a vehicle carries a group's id rather than each state's

limits_start_on.description: The day its speed and power limits take effect, when a law not yet in force sets them; its rules carry their own dates

throttle.description: Whether the motor may propel it without the rider pedaling

class_3_throttle.description: False where its law bars a Class 3 from having a throttle at all; left out, a Class 3's throttle has to stop at 20 mph

e_bike_law.description: A jurisdiction's whole e-bike law rather than one class or tier of it, so it goes on a vehicle's assist mode though it allows a throttle

max_speed.description: The fastest the motor may propel it, in kilometers per hour

max_throttle_speed.description: The fastest the motor may propel it on its own, without the rider pedaling, in kilometers per hour

min_power.description: The motor power it's above; a horsepower limit converts at 750 W per hp, as federal law and California's statute do, in watts

max_power.description: The motor's power limit; restrictions say whether it's inclusive, and a horsepower limit converts at 750 W per hp, in watts

categories.description: What it covers: rider_rule what the rider or owner does, registration and insurance included; seller_rule what its maker, dealer or seller does; vehicle_definition what the vehicle is or must have; enforcement penalties, impound and police powers; legal_context the law around the rules rather than one anyone follows, like a repeal, a gap, a ruling, an undated bill or a duty on governments, motorists or landowners; top_rule_0, top_rule_1, and top_rule_2, each on at most one of a classification's rules and never on a vehicle_definition that isn't also a rider_rule, what a rider whose vehicle is in it most needs to know and wouldn't assume, most important first, never common sense like a helmet, a sidewalk ban or a local authority, agency or land manager being able to ban or allow it, though a default ban one has to lift counts

jurisdiction.description: The narrower place it applies: an area, with a US county's or Census place's FIPS code after its state (US-CA-081, US-NY-51000), and a :land_type (US:national_park); it holds in every area whose code starts with it, and a rule without one wherever its classification does

citation.description: The statute, regulation or bill that states it, e.g. California Vehicle Code §312.5

starts_on.description: The day it takes effect; a rule without one is in force now

sources.description: Pages that back the classification as a whole; a page that states one of its rules goes on that rule instead
